groups.text: Yang’s ambition was to get an architect’s certificate or become a bowling master. But when he was conducting experiments with a microscope in the basement, a tank on the bench exploded, sending him flying outwards through the exit. He was out of breath while knowing he lost his eyesight as well as 70% of his hearing.
groups.zh: 杨的志向是取得建筑师资格证，或成为保龄球高手。但当他在地下室里用显微镜做实验时，工作台上的一个罐子爆炸了，将他从出口炸飞了出去。他感到喘不过气来，因为得知自己失去了视力，以及70%的听力。

groups.text: In other words, he was disabled. Feeling clumsy, he was annoyed at first though nobody made fun of him. He cut out going outdoors and just sat around at home talking to his parrot or tortoise silently.
groups.zh: 换句话说，他成了残障人士。起初他觉得自己笨拙，十分烦躁，尽管没人取笑他。他不再外出，只是整天在家闲坐，默默地对着鹦鹉或乌龟说话。

groups.text: His sister resigned to help him in many ways. Her assistance and encouragement were so beneficial to his psychology that he adapted to his disability soon and became outgoing again. In a college accessible to him, he studied politics and literature.
groups.zh: 姐姐辞了职，从多方面帮助他。她的帮助和鼓励对他的心理状态十分有益，以至于他很快适应了自己的残障状况，又变得开朗起来。在一所方便他就读的大学里，他学习政治和文学。

groups.text: He always sat in the front row near the entry without any absence and, with the help of his handy laptop, he studied well by means of dictation. His thesis, Abolishing Slavery, met with all professors’ approval. After class, he and his companions often played drum music, which was noisy but suitable for his hearing.
groups.zh: 他总坐在靠近入口的前排，从不缺席，而且，借助方便使用的笔记本电脑，他通过听写学习，学得很好。他的论文《废除奴隶制》，得到了所有教授的认可。课后，他经常和同伴一起敲鼓演奏，声音虽然大，却适合他的听力状况。

groups.text: After graduation, he made high profits by designing software for a firm. All in all, in his community, he won his dignity and people’s congratulations. He always wished all the best to his disabled fellows and encouraged them, “Never mind!
groups.zh: 毕业后，他通过为一家公司设计软件获得了丰厚收益。总而言之，在他所在的社区里，他赢得了自己的尊严，也赢得了人们的祝贺。他总把最好的祝愿送给其他残障伙伴，鼓励他们说：“别灰心！

groups.text: All you have is adequate to achieve your goals.”
groups.zh: 你所拥有的一切，足以帮助你实现目标。”
